title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 197 (Overall maximum managerial remuneration and managerial remuneration in case of absence or inadequacy of profits)

content.overview: Section 197 caps the total managerial remuneration payable by a public company to its directors, including managing director and whole-time director, and its manager in respect of any financial year at eleven per cent of the net profits of that company for that financial year computed in the manner laid down in section 198, except that the company in general meeting may, with the approval of the Central Government where required by the rules in force, authorise payment of remuneration exceeding eleven per cent. Individual ceilings apply within that overall limit. Where in any financial year a company has no profits or its profits are inadequate, it may pay remuneration in accordance with Schedule V, subject to the conditions stated. Excess remuneration is recoverable from the person who received it. Sitting fees are dealt with separately under the section.
content.glance: Public company: total managerial remuneration ≤ 11% of net profits (s. 198); GM may authorise more (CG approval where rules require); individual ceilings for MD/WTD/manager and other directors; inadequate profits → Schedule V route; excess recoverable; sitting fees separate.
content.study: The total managerial remuneration payable by a public company to its directors, including managing director and whole-time director, and its manager in respect of any financial year shall not exceed eleven per cent of the net profits of that company for that financial year computed in the manner laid down in section 198 except that the company in general meeting may, authorise the payment of remuneration exceeding eleven per cent of the net profits of the company, subject to the provisions of Schedule V. The remuneration payable to any one managing director or whole-time director or manager shall not exceed five per cent of the net profits, and if there is more than one such director, remuneration shall not exceed ten per cent of the net profits to all such directors and manager taken together. Remuneration payable to directors who are neither managing directors nor whole-time directors shall not exceed one per cent of the net profits of the company if there is a managing or whole-time director or manager, and three per cent in any other case. Where in any financial year a company has no profits or its profits are inadequate, the company shall not pay to its directors, including managing or whole-time director or manager, any remuneration exclusive of sitting fees except in accordance with the provisions of Schedule V. If any director draws or receives, directly or indirectly, by way of remuneration any such sums in excess of the limit, he shall refund such sums to the company and until such sum is refunded, hold it in trust for the company. Current-law framing: compute net profits under s. 198; apply 11% overall and individual ceilings; test special resolution/Schedule V path for excess or inadequate profits; apply recovery of excess.

sections.heading: Overall Ceiling
sections.body: Public company: total managerial remuneration to directors (including MD/WTD) and manager ≤ 11% of net profits computed under s. 198, unless GM authorises more subject to Schedule V / rules.

sections.heading: Individual Ceilings
sections.body: One MD/WTD/manager ≤ 5%; more than one such persons together ≤ 10%; other directors ≤ 1% (if there is MD/WTD/manager) or 3% (otherwise).

sections.heading: Inadequate Profits
sections.body: No profits or inadequate profits: remuneration (exclusive of sitting fees) only in accordance with Schedule V.

sections.heading: Recovery of Excess
sections.body: Excess remuneration is refundable to the company and held in trust until refunded.

provisions.title: Overall maximum managerial remuneration and managerial remuneration in case of absence or inadequacy of profits

examples.title: Exceeding 11%
examples.body: A public company’s net profits under s. 198 are ₹10 crore. Total managerial remuneration proposed is ₹1.5 crore (15%). Without GM authorisation under the section and applicable Schedule V conditions, the payment exceeds the 11% ceiling.

examples.title: Inadequate profits
examples.body: A public company has inadequate profits in a year. It may still pay MD remuneration only in accordance with Schedule V conditions, not by freely exceeding the percentage ceilings.

hypotheticals.question: Does Board approval alone allow managerial pay above 11% of net profits?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Exceeding the overall 11% ceiling requires authorisation by the company in general meeting, subject to Schedule V and any Central Government approval the rules in force require. Board approval is not enough.

distinctions.title: Managerial remuneration (s. 197) vs appointment of MD/WTD/manager (s. 196)
distinctions.right: Who may be appointed and for how long

misconceptions.trap: Private companies are freely subject to the same 11% ceiling as public companies under s. 197.
misconceptions.correction: Section 197’s overall and individual percentage ceilings are framed for public companies. Private-company treatment follows the Act and any applicable exemptions; do not assume the public-company ceiling applies automatically.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 197 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Compute net profits under s. 198. II. Apply 11% and individual ceilings. III. Test GM/Schedule V path if exceeded or profits inadequate. IV. Apply recovery of excess. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Profit computation; ceilings; approval path; excess recovery; precise relief.

examTips: Excess held in trust and recoverable.
